title.narrative: PERFORMANCE-BASED PARTNERSHIP SCHEME FOCUSING ON QUALITY PROGRAMMING, UNDERSTANDING CHANGE AND RESULTS FOR POOR HOUSEHOLDS AND COMMUNITIES

description.narrative: The programme Food and Nutrition Security through Equitable and Climate Smart Food Systems will work in Port Loko and Tonkolili North Western Province, Sierra Leone. It aims to contribute to Concern Sierra Leone's Food Systems for Food Security thematic programme, and the goal of the grant is to ensure vulnerable households' resilience to food and nutrition insecurity is increased by strengthening food systems. The programme will support over 86,310 people living in extreme poor households including those headed by women, households with disabled members, out of school young people, pregnant and lactating women, and people living with HIV. This will be done through better and more inclusive community management of natural resources, adoption of inclusive climate smart food production practices, profitable marketing of foods and food products, and improved access to quality productive assets.. OVERALL COUNTRY PROG: To provide inclusive climate resilient and environmentally sustainable livelihood opportunities to vulnerable populations in Banadir and Somaliland. SPECIFIC OUTCOME: RM Adaptation 2: Outputs (particularly output 2.2 and 2.3) under this outcome are focused on the promotion of sustainable climate-resilient farming methods and increasing access to climate-resilient seeds These are eligible for a Rio Marker scoring of two under adaptation – (AGRICULTURE – 311, p.22 CM handbook). DRR 1: Focusing on agricultural markets and investment by linking rural food producers to the private sector builds resilience of households and communities, ultimately reducing humanitarian needs sustainably.Aid to the environment 1: CSA and landscape management approaches promoted under the FS4FS support the protection of natural resources.Capacity Building 1: This outcome includes a variety of capacity strengthening activities, e.g. business and vocational trainings, financial resources (saving groups, microfinance); market mapping, price monitoring, input fairs, quality seeds.Gender Equality 1: This outcome supports inclusive economic growth around agriculture, especially for women.Nutrition 1: This outcome focuses on access to markets and food as well as the economic status of HHS, thus improving the nutritional status of HHS.
